::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Hide custom environment content based on boolean](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/15509/hide-custom-environment-content-based-on-boolean), asked by [Santiago Palladino](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/4805/santiago-palladino) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-04-11; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I have a custom environment which adds some text around its content, but I also want it to be able to show or hide its contents depending on a boolean. 
>
> I have tried doing the following:
>
> ```latex
> \newif\ifshow
> \showfalse
> \newenvironment{myenv}
> {\ifshow\textbf{Content of myenv:}}
> {\fi}
> ```
>
> But the first `\begin{myenv}` raises an `Incomplete \iffalse; all text was ignored after line X`. It would seem that the `\iffalse` is causing the `\end{myenv}` to be ignored, so the `\fi` is never written.
>
> Any idea on how could I accomplish this?
:::

Another way to do this is to use the [`environ`](http://ctan.org/pkg/environ) package and conditionally keep or toss the `\BODY`.

```latex
\usepackage{environ}
\NewEnviron{myenv}{
  \ifshow
    \textbf{Content of myenv: \BODY}
  \fi}
```
